Yes. Three separate things exist; only one of them actually removes the prompt tax.

## The flag that removes it: `--system-prompt`

`--system-prompt <text>` doesn't *append* — it swaps the template. `system-prompt.ts:1033` picks `custom-system-prompt.md` instead of `system-prompt.md` when a custom prompt resolves, so the entire base prompt (Role, Engineering, Workflow, Tool Policy, Delivery, Critical) is gone. The wrapper that survives only emits `{{customPrompt}}` plus optional blocks: context files, git snapshot, skills, rules, secrets note.

Measured floor (same method as before, provider-reported `usage.input`):

| Configuration | cwd | Input tokens |
|---|---|---|
| default | `~/Projects` | 24,507 |
| `--no-skills --no-rules --no-tools --no-extensions --system-prompt " "` | `~/Projects` | 1,774 |
| same, in an empty dir | `/tmp/bare-ctx` | **590** (545 non-message) |

The 1,774 → 590 drop is your `AGENTS.md` chain plus the git snapshot — those live in the *wrapper*, not the base prompt, so they load even with a custom prompt. Running from a non-repo directory with no `AGENTS.md` is what kills them. 545 tokens is the irreducible floor: date/cwd reminder and framing.

`--system-prompt " "` (a space, not `""`) is required — `title-generator.ts:162` does `?.trim() || undefined`, and an empty string falls back to the default in some paths. A space passes the `!== undefined` check at `sdk.ts:1455`.

## Interactive headless, three ways

1. **`-p --continue` loop** — verified: turn 1 = 590 tokens, turn 2 = 604, `nonMessageTokens` stays 545 and the model recalled "41" across processes. Each call is a fresh process reading the session JSONL; overhead never re-inflates. Cheapest for scripted test iteration.
2. **`--mode rpc` / `rpc-ui`** — JSON-RPC over stdio, one long-lived process, genuinely interactive, no TUI.
3. **`buddha acp`** — Agent Client Protocol server over stdio, for editor-style clients.

`buddha shell` is *not* this — it's a shell console, not an agent session.

## What the other flags do and don't do

- `--no-tools` removes tool schemas (the ~15.9k half of your earlier accounting) but nothing from the prompt.
- `--no-skills` / `--no-rules` only blank the wrapper's skills/rules blocks; with a custom prompt they're near-free, but harmless to keep.
- Skills disabled alone was 18,982; the 590 figure needs `--system-prompt` — no `--no-system-prompt` flag exists.


## Architecture decision you should know about

Recon (`agent://RpcRecon`) killed the RPC-first plan. RPC mode is JSONL over stdio with a custom envelope — **not** JSON-RPC — and its `RpcCommand` union (`src/modes/rpc/rpc-types.ts:29-101`) has **no per-request system prompt, model, tool-restriction, or outputSchema**. Those are launch-time only (`main.ts:1071` maps `--system-prompt` → `options.customSystemPrompt`). Four stage prompts would mean four separate RPC processes and still no structured-output control.

So: **OMP SDK** (`createAgentSession`, `sdk.ts:1330`), which your spec explicitly permits when "materially simpler". **Reconnect is server-pushed, not client-replayed.** On every socket open, if a run is in flight the server immediately pushes a snapshot (`run_started`, then per-stage latest `stage_started` / delta tail / `stage_completed`) before any new live frames.
